 Eagles lead Ireland in historic series 
 by Helge Schutz 
 Gerhard Erasmus in action for Namibia. File photo 
 The FNB Namibian Eagles completed a second successive victory against Ireland on Tuesday to take a 2-1 lead in their five match series. 
 Ireland won the first encounter on 22 October by 55 runs, but Namibia struck back in style with two emphatic victories.
 On 24 October they beat Ireland by 31 runs, making history in the process by recording their first-ever win against a test-playing nation.
 Namibia posted a total 321 for six wickets off their 50 overs before dismissing Ireland for 290 all out.
 Captain Gerhard Erasmus led the way with a superb knock of 156 not out off 125 balls (14×4, 4×6), while Jan Frylinck added 76.
 Erasmus’ knock was the joint second highest ever by a batter from an associate nation, just behind Scotland’s Callum McLeod, who scored 157 against Afghanistan, and alongside Scotland’s Kyle Coetzer, who scored 156 against Bangladesh.
 In Ireland’s innings, Jack Brassell shone with the ball, taking four wickets for 52 runs, while Erasmus took 2/13 to win the man of the match award.
 On Tuesday, it was Frylinck’s turn to lead Namibia’s onslaught as their batters once again laid a solid platform by scoring 316 for seven wickets.
 Frylinck led the way with a great century, as he scored 126 off 122 balls (9×4, 4×6) to complete his third century in One Day International (ODI) cricket, while he also passed 1 500 ODI runs in the process.
 After winning the toss and electing to bat, Namibia lost Louren Steenkamp for 13, but Frylinck and Malan Kruger revived the innings with a 48-run partnership before Kruger was caught and bowled by Andy McBrine for 42 off 46 balls (6×4).
 Erasmus joined Frylinck and put Namibia in charge with a 102-run partnership off only 79 balls.
 Erasmus was eventually out for 54 off 51 balls (6×4, 1×6) but Frylinck went on to reach his century, while Alex Volschenk added 36 off 26 balls (2×4, 3×6) as Namibia posted another impressive total.
 Ireland’s run chase suffered a premature blow when captain Paul Stirling had to retire with an injured finger while fielding, and spinner Bernard Scholtz immediately added to the pressure when he trapped Cade Carmichael lbw for a duck in the first over, with only one run on the board.
 Namibia’s bowlers continued to make inroads with Ruben Trumpelmann dismissing Andrew Balbirnie for 20, and Brassel bowling Lorcan Tucker for 26, and when Trumpelman bowled Harry Tector for six, Ireland were struggling at 56/4.
 GREAT KNOCK BY CAMPHER
 Curtis Campher and McBrine revived Ireland’s innings with a 61-run partnership, before Scholtz dismissed McBrine for 30, but Campher kept Ireland’s hopes alive with a great knock.
 He went on to reach his half century off 45 balls, and when he reached his century off 82 balls in the 41st over, Ireland were still well in the game at 233 for six wickets.
 Campher’s innings, however, came to an end two overs later when he was run out by Kruger for 106 runs off 86 balls (11×4, 3×6), which effectively ended Ireland’s hopes.
 George Dockrell added 25 and Gavin Hoey 21 further down the order before the whole side was dismissed for 253 – still 63 runs short of the target.
 Namibia’s top bowlers were Scholtz (2/31), Trumpelmann ()2/37) and Brassell (2/72).
 Namibia’s victory put them 2-1 up in the series and in the driving seat to complete a first ever series victory against a Test-playing nation.
 Namibia coach Craig Williams says he was happy with the win but a lot of work still lay ahead.
 “I think we played really well in certain areas and the fact that another batter in our top four got a century, allowed us to set up quite a good score, so we are really happy with the win.
 “To go 2-1 up in the series puts us in a good position, obviously, so with two games left to play, we need to reset very quickly. We’ve played really good cricket over the last couple of months, we’ve put in a hell of a lot of work, and we’d love to get a series win. We’ll enjoy tonight but tomorrow morning we must reset and just look at what we can do better,” he adds.
 Williams says they didn’t really celebrate much after their historic first ever win against a test playing nation on 24 October.
 “With all due respect to Ireland, we didn’t celebrate that much because we actually didn’t play a good game. So, we were more disappointed in the way we played. But, yeah, to get that first win under the belt against Test nation just shows what we are capable of,” he says.
 “We’ve been really good in some areas but there’s certain areas that we haven’t been good at, so we will regroup, we’ll do our analysis and see what we can do better,” he adds.
 “Ireland are an extremely good team. You can’t take anything for granted against them and they’ll do their homework, so we’ve just got to get better. If we can play our best in all three departments, I think we stand a really good chance of taking a series win,” he says.
